title: PepsiCo Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply
summary: Everything you need to land a PepsiCo internship in 2027–2028, programs, eligibility, deadlines, the interview process, and tips to stand out.
body_text: PepsiCo Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply Last updated: July 2026 PepsiCo hires over 1,500 interns across North America every summer , one of the largest intern classes in consumer goods, and more than 50% convert to full-time employees . For the 2027 cycle, applications are expected to open around late August 2026, mirroring the documented pattern where the 2026 window ran August 25 to October 31, 2025. That gives you roughly a two-month window to apply, but PepsiCo reviews applications on a rolling basis and fills positions before the posted deadline. Wait until October and the strongest seats are already spoken for. Quick Facts Fact Detail Where to apply pepsicojobs.com/internshipsprograms . Join the Talent Community for opening alerts Application window (2027) Expected late August to late October 2026 for summer 2027 (documented pattern from 2026 cycle: Aug 25–Oct 31, 2025) Rolling? Effectively yes. Positions fill as strong candidates apply; PepsiCo recommends applying within the first 1–2 weeks Eligibility Penultimate-year undergrad or grad student; 3.0 GPA minimum for most tracks (3.2 for e-commerce/sales-marketing); authorized to work in the US Duration 10 to 12 weeks (May/June through August); co-ops run a full semester Compensation $20–$37/hr depending on role and location; supply chain interns at Frito-Lay report $33/hr plus a $2,250 housing stipend Return offers Official: more than 50% of North American interns convert to full-time employees Locations Purchase NY (HQ), Plano TX (Frito-Lay), Chicago IL (Quaker/Gatorade), plus field locations nationwide for Sales # Programs 7 career areas with 15+ distinct internship tracks in the US, plus MBA-specific and global programs The numbers that matter: a two-month window expected to open late August 2026 for summer 2027, rolling review that fills seats before the deadline, and an official 50%+ conversion rate. PepsiCo posts a 3.0 GPA floor for most tracks, lower than some banks but real enough to check. Externships are short, remote professional experience programs where you finish a real project with a real company. The Amazon Fulfillment Center Operational Strategy Externship and the Beats by Dre Consumer Behavior & Market Analysis Externship build exactly the operations and consumer-insights evidence a late-August application needs. Explore all Externships . What Is a PepsiCo Internship? A PepsiCo internship is a paid, 10-to-12-week summer placement that puts over 1,500 college students into real roles across seven career areas, from supply chain and marketing to finance, R&D, and technology, at PepsiCo offices around the US. The numbers back the reputation up: interns rate the program 4.4 out of 5 on Glassdoor with 82% recommending it, and LinkedIn named PepsiCo a Top Company in 2023, 2024, and 2026. PepsiCo is the #44 company on the Fortune 500 with $93.9 billion in revenue and 65+ brands including Pepsi, Lay's, Gatorade, Doritos, and Quaker Oats. Globally, more than 4,000 interns join every year. When Do PepsiCo Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028? PepsiCo's calendar is documented and tight: the summer 2026 cycle opened August 25, 2025, and closed October 31, 2025, a two-month window. Interviews and the PepHire assessment run on a rolling basis inside that window, with offers going out as early as November and hiring effectively wrapped by January. For summer 2027, you apply in fall 2026, about 10 months before the June start. that's faster than banking calendars but standard for CPG. And because PepsiCo fills positions as candidates clear the process, a week-one application faces the most open seats. Now · July 2026 you're HERE The summer 2027 window is roughly a month away. Applications for summer 2026 opened August 25, and PepsiCo is expected to follow the same pattern. This is the last stretch to build resume proof before the portal goes live. The Amazon Fulfillment Center Operational Strategy Externship and the Beats by Dre Consumer Behavior Externship are remote, real-company projects that give a late-August application finished work to point at. Late August 2026 ROLLING — APPLY WEEK 1 The summer 2027 window is expected to open here and run about two months through late October. Review is rolling, so a week-one application meets the most open seats across all seven career areas. September to December 2026 Rolling process: pre-screening questions, PepHire assessment (cognitive, situational judgment, and personality tests) for some roles, then one to three interview rounds. PepsiCo evaluates against its GREAT5 leadership framework. Offers start going out as early as November. Summer 2027 10 to 12 weeks, May/June through August. Over 1,500 interns across North America, seven career areas, and more than 50% convert to full-time roles. Late August 2027 EXPECTED The summer 2028 window is expected to open here, following the same late-August-to-late-October pattern. If you miss the 2027 cycle, this is your next shot. Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open PepsiCo's own careers page makes it clear: positions are filled as strong candidates apply, and the application window is only about two months long. Forage's PepsiCo guide confirms that positions fill before posted deadlines. Rolling review inside a two-month window means the class shrinks while the portal is still open. Most applicants treat late October like the real deadline, but by then recruiters have been interviewing for weeks and the strongest seats, especially in supply chain and technology, are spoken for. Submit in the first two weeks of the window, and you compete with the smallest applicant pool for the largest number of open seats. Which PepsiCo Internship Programs Should You Target? PepsiCo offers internships across seven career areas with 15+ distinct tracks in the US. The split depends on whether you want to build things (supply chain, R&D, technology), sell things (marketing, sales), or manage the numbers behind them (finance, procurement). Program Focus Duration Key skills Supply Chain (Frito-Lay/PBNA) Production, warehouse ops, transportation, planning, commercialization 10–12 weeks Operations, logistics, data analysis, leadership Marketing (Undergrad) Brand positioning, product launch, digital campaigns, consumer research 10 weeks Research, storytelling, data-driven insights, consumer behavior Finance (Strategic Finance/Audit) FP&A, cost analysis, financial reporting, audit, M&A support 10–12 weeks Excel, PowerPoint, analytical skills; 2 accounting courses required Technology (SWE/Data Science) Software engineering, data analytics, cybersecurity, e-commerce BI 10–12 weeks Python, SQL, data visualization, Agile/Scrum Sales Customer-facing projects, sales metrics, promotions, brand development 10–12 weeks Customer service, presentations, work ethic; driver's license required R&D Food science, packaging engineering, product development, quality, sensory 10–12 weeks Lab/pilot plant skills, food science, engineering, technical knowledge See all programs at pepsicojobs.com/internshipsprograms . MBA-specific tracks in Marketing and Global Procurement have their own posting windows and prefer 3+ years of work experience. PepsiCo also offers co-ops (full semester, four months) and a Forage virtual experience for early exploration. What Are the Eligibility Requirements? PepsiCo posts consistent requirements across its US internship tracks: • Enrollment: penultimate-year undergraduate or graduate student graduating within one year after the internship ends. MBA roles (Marketing MBA, Global Procurement) require MBA graduation within one year and prefer 3+ years of prior work experience. • GPA: 3.0 minimum on a 4.0 scale for most tracks. E-commerce and sales-marketing roles require 3.2. Some field positions set the bar at 2.75. There is no single company-wide cutoff. • Coursework: the Finance track specifically requires at least two college-level accounting courses, regardless of GPA. • Work authorization: most postings require US work authorization without current or future employer sponsorship. CPT and OPT don't require employer sponsorship. PepsiCo filed 45 LCAs in FY2025, so some roles may offer H-1B sponsorship, but assume the default answer is no unless a posting says otherwise. • Driver's license: Sales and food-service internships require a valid US driver's license (at least 3 months before start) and access to a car. • Availability: the full 10 to 12 weeks on PepsiCo's schedule. Does PepsiCo Have a Hard GPA Cutoff? Yes, and it's published: 3.0 for most tracks, 3.2 for e-commerce and sales-marketing, and 2.75 for some field roles. That makes PepsiCo more explicit than many competitors. If your cumulative GPA is below 3.0, target the field roles with the 2.75 floor or build it up before applying. The Finance track adds another gate: at least two college-level accounting courses, which means a spring-semester sophomore who hasn't taken accounting yet needs to plan coursework around the fall application window. What Skills Does PepsiCo Look For, and How Do You Build Them? PepsiCo's 10 surviving US internship track descriptions share a backbone of soft skills wrapped around the GREAT5 leadership framework, Growth, Relationships, Execution, Agility, Thinking. Communication appears in virtually every posting. Analytical and problem-solving skills show up across supply chain, finance, R&D, and technology. But the technical asks stay track-specific: Finance wants Excel and accounting coursework, Technology lists Python, SQL, and Agile, and R&D expects food science or engineering lab skills. What does that pattern tell you? PepsiCo hires people who can communicate, lead, and analyze, then trains the vertical. What PepsiCo looks for in interns Skills across 10 PepsiCo intern & analyst job descriptions · 2026-cycle internship track JDs, projecting 2027–2028 Communication & presenting 9 of 10 Analytical & problem solving 7 of 10 Leadership & initiative 6 of 10 Data analysis & reporting 5 of 10 Cross-functional collaboration 4 of 10 Strategic & critical thinking 4 of 10 Organization & time management 3 of 10 Customer & consumer focus 3 of 10 Method: full-text analysis of PepsiCo's 10 surviving 2026-cycle US internship track descriptions (Supply Chain, Marketing Undergrad, Marketing MBA, Finance, Supply Chain Finance, Technology, Sales, R&D, Global Procurement, HR/Health & Safety) via pepsicojobs.com and job-board mirrors. Prior-cycle basis; counts skew toward the soft skills all tracks share. How Is Demand for CPG and Supply Chain Interns Moving Right Now? CPG and supply chain intern hiring right now: July 2026 Across US supply chain and CPG intern postings tracked this week · aggregate market data, all employers ▲ Supply chain intern demand is elevated: ongoing reshoring and automation investment keep logistics and operations roles consistently posted, and the CPG sector leads volume ★ Data skills carry a premium: data-analytics and data-science intern postings in CPG advertise measurably higher hourly rates than general operations roles = Entry-level CPG pipeline is deep: PepsiCo alone hires 1,500+ interns in North America, and peer firms (Coca-Cola, P&G, Unilever, Nestlé) run comparably sized programs The signal is volume: CPG companies are absorbing interns at scale because the supply-chain and digital-marketing talent pipelines feed their most critical functions. The data-skilled end of the market commands higher pay. Method: directional analysis of US CPG and supply chain intern postings, July 2026. PepsiCo hiring volumes are from pepsicojobs.com; peer-firm sizing is from Glassdoor and company careers pages. Build These Skills Before You Apply And every skill in the chart maps to a remote Externship where you finish a real company project before the window opens. Skill (from real JDs) JD evidence Externship that builds it Supply chain operations & logistics Supply Chain JD: production, warehouse ops, transportation, planning, commercialization Amazon Fulfillment Center Operational Strategy & People Analytics Consumer behavior & brand strategy Marketing JD: brand positioning, product launch, digital campaigns, consumer research Beats by Dre Consumer Behavior & Market Analysis Financial modeling & valuation Finance JD: FP&A, cost analysis, DCF models, capital analytics Attronica FP&A & Private Company Valuation How close is the overlap? The Amazon Externship delivers operational strategy work in the Supply Chain posting's own vocabulary, and the client-ready analysis every Externship ends on is the "communication and presenting recommendations" line item nine of ten JDs share. What Is the PepsiCo Application and Interview Process Like? PepsiCo's funnel has more steps than a typical CPG firm but moves fast, averaging about 15 days from application to decision according to Glassdoor: 1. Find your track at pepsicojobs.com using the career-area filter. PepsiCo's recruiting chatbot (Chester Cheetah) can help match roles. Upload your resume and fill out the application questions through Candidate Zone. 2. Pre-screening. Some roles send text-based pre-screening questions or one-way video prompts before any human contact. Answer promptly; delays here can drop you from rolling review. 3. PepHire assessment. Not required for every track, but when it appears, expect a Wonderlic-style cognitive test (50 questions in 12 minutes), a situational judgment test, and a personality assessment aligned with the GREAT5 framework. 4. One to three interview rounds , a phone or video screen with a recruiter, then one or two rounds with the hiring manager and team. Behavioral STAR-method questions dominate, framed around the GREAT5 principles: Growth, Relationships, Execution, Agility, Thinking. 5. Offer via Candidate Zone. Glassdoor rates intern interview difficulty at 2.8 out of 5, with 75% positive experiences. The PepHire assessment is the wildcard. PepsiCo doesn't publish its specs, but third-party prep sites describe the cognitive section as time-pressured (about 14 seconds per question). Practice timed aptitude tests before the window opens, and rehearse your GREAT5 stories in STAR format: our HireVue question guide with a free AI mock tool runs the same behavioral pressure. What Students on Reddit Say Three threads show the process from the inside. Great place to work. Always opportunities to move up and work in different departments and geographies. Most interns can end up getting a full-time offer if they do well. r/supplychain employee perspective, paraphrased · read the thread PepsiCo Supply Chain Intern at Frito-Lay. Pay: $33 an hour plus a $2,250 housing stipend. The commute was long, but the experience and pay made up for it. r/internships intern report, paraphrased · read the thread I interviewed and accepted an offer for the supply chain program. My best tip for the second round is to connect with the interviewer on something personal. Be genuine. r/Pepsi incoming intern, paraphrased · read the thread How Do You Stand Out When 1,500 Seats Fill on a Rolling Basis? Three moves, all executable before late August. First, apply in week one of the window; rolling review with positions filling before the deadline makes timing the cheapest advantage you have. Second, match the GREAT5 framework in your application: Growth (show curiosity), Relationships (show authenticity), Execution (show energy), Agility (show adaptability), Thinking (show strategic insight). PepsiCo evaluates every candidate against these five principles, so your stories should map to them. Third, show up with proof in the JD's exact language. A finished supply-chain operations project or a consumer-behavior analysis answers "tell me about a time you solved a problem" with an artifact instead of an anecdote. And remember the official conversion rate is 50%+. Interview like someone auditioning for the full-time seat, because you're. What Other Companies Should You Consider? PepsiCo's peer set splits by what you want: a rival CPG with similar scale, or a company with a different product category but the same career tracks. Coca-Cola direct rival in beverages; similar supply chain and marketing tracks, comparable intern class size Careers site Procter & Gamble CPG leader in household goods; one of the most competitive intern programs in the industry Careers site Unilever global CPG with a strong sustainability brand and European-headquartered culture Careers site Nestlé world's largest food company by revenue; strong R&D and supply chain tracks Careers site All four hire at scale, and their application windows overlap with PepsiCo's late-August-to-October season. Apply broadly across the CPG set, but tailor each application to the company's leadership framework, PepsiCo's GREAT5 is specific enough that recycled answers will read flat. FAQ Can I still apply for a PepsiCo summer 2027 internship? Not yet, and you haven't missed it. PepsiCo's summer 2026 cycle opened August 25, 2025, and the summer 2027 window is expected to follow the same pattern, opening around late August 2026. Join the Talent Community at pepsicojobs.com for the alert, then apply in week one. When do PepsiCo internship applications open for summer 2028? Expected around late August 2027, based on PepsiCo's documented late-August-to-late-October pattern. that's roughly 10 months before the June 2028 start. The window runs about two months, and positions fill before the posted deadline. Is PepsiCo internship recruiting rolling? Effectively yes. PepsiCo reviews applications as they come in and fills positions before posted deadlines. The window is only about two months, so submitting within the first one to two weeks gives you the best chance. Offers start going out as early as November. What GPA do you need for a PepsiCo internship? Most tracks require a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. E-commerce and sales-marketing roles ask for 3.2, and a few field positions set the bar at 2.75. Finance roles also require at least two college-level accounting courses regardless of GPA. What is the PepsiCo interview and assessment process like? After applying, you may receive pre-screening text questions or one-way video prompts. Some roles include a PepHire assessment with cognitive, situational judgment, and personality tests. You then move to one to three interview rounds. PepsiCo evaluates candidates against its GREAT5 leadership framework using STAR-method behavioral questions. Glassdoor rates difficulty at 2.8 out of 5. Do PepsiCo interns get return offers? PepsiCo's official careers page says more than 50% of North American interns convert to full-time roles. Forage reports 89.5% of program finishers stay two or more years. Reddit feedback is mixed by year and division, but strong performers who show the GREAT5 principles have the best odds. What skills does PepsiCo look for in interns? Across 10 US internship tracks: communication (9 of 10), analytical and problem solving (7 of 10), and leadership (6 of 10), plus track-specific asks like Python and SQL for Technology, Excel and accounting for Finance, and food science for R&D. PepsiCo evaluates everyone on its GREAT5 framework: Growth, Relationships, Execution, Agility, Thinking. Are PepsiCo internships paid? Most US summer internships are paid, with hourly rates ranging from about $20 for sales roles to $37 for software engineering at Frito-Lay in Plano, TX. Supply chain interns at Frito-Lay report $33 per hour plus a $2,250 housing stipend. Pay is non-negotiable and based on role, degree level, and location. The window is two months long and the review inside it's rolling. Spend the runway building proof: a remote Externship turns "interested in supply chain" into a finished operations project a late-August application can point at. About the Author Bifei Wang has spent 17 years focused on human flow and the growth of young professionals, spanning international education, career training and coaching, and recruitment process outsourcing. Over 7 years at Extern, he has had one-on-one sessions with thousands of students exploring careers in consulting, finance, tech, marketing, and data, giving him a firsthand view of how the job market has shifted for early-career professionals and what it actually takes to break in.

title: Vertiv appoints Frieda He as chief procurement officer
summary: Frieda He was named Vertiv's Chief Procurement Officer effective May 5, 2026, with global responsibility for leading the company's procurement organization across direct and indirect materials, supplier quality, cost management, and supply chain resilience in support of Vertiv's worldwide growth and operations.
body_text: COLUMBUS, Ohio [May 5, 2026] — Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global leader in critical digital infrastructure, today announced Frieda He has joined the company as Chief Procurement Officer (CPO). She will lead Vertiv’s global procurement organization, with a focus on further strengthening supply chain resilience, enabling growth, optimizing cost and value, and driving supplier quality across the company’s portfolio, including end‑to‑end power and thermal management solutions for data centers, communications networks, and commercial & industrial applications. Frieda brings nearly two decades of global procurement and supply chain leadership experience across the automotive and electrification businesses. In her most recent role, from December 2023 to March 2026, Frieda served as Chief Procurement Officer and a member of the Group Management Team at Polestar. She oversaw more than $3 billion in annual global spend across direct and indirect materials, supplier quality, R&D industrial programs, cost management, and global real estate, while leading cross-functional global teams and driving cost savings, governance, and enterprise transformation during periods of industry disruption. “Frieda He is a proven global leader with deep experience building and scaling resilient, sustainable supply chains,” said Gio Albertazzi, chief executive officer, Vertiv. “Her expertise in complex, multinational procurement environments and her track record of driving operational discipline and value creation will be critical as Vertiv continues to scale to meet accelerating demand from AI‑driven and high‑density digital infrastructure.” Prior to Polestar, Frieda held a series of senior leadership roles at Volvo Cars, including vice president, head of global propulsion & sustainability procurement, where she led a more than $9 billion annual spend organization and played a key role in the company’s electrification transformation. Her experience includes managing supply chains through global disruptions, strengthening supplier quality and capability, advancing sustainability and regulatory compliance, and supporting major structural transactions and joint ventures. Earlier in her career, she held procurement and supply chain roles in China and across the Asia‑Pacific region, building deep expertise in global sourcing, cost engineering, and supplier development. “I’m excited to join Vertiv at such a transformative moment for the digital infrastructure industry,” said Frieda He. “Vertiv’s role at the center of the global data center and critical infrastructure ecosystem presents a unique opportunity to create value through strong partnerships, operational excellence, and responsible, resilient supply chains.” Frieda holds bachelor’s degrees in general studies and business/commerce from Northeast Normal University in China, and an Executive MBA from the University of Oxford in England. About Vertiv Vertiv (NYSE: VRT) brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to enable its customers’ vital applications to run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs. Vertiv solves the most important challenges facing today’s data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities with a portfolio of power, cooling and IT infrastructure solutions and services that extends from the cloud to the edge of the network. Headquartered in Westerville, Ohio, USA, Vertiv does business in more than 130 countries. For more information, and for the latest news and content from Vertiv, visit Vertiv.com . title: How Valve and Fitting Distributors Finance Cross-Border Inventory Through Laredo
summary: Valve and fitting importer financing in Texas: how distributors moving inventory through Laredo cover vendor payments before the truck clears the bridge. How Va
body_text: How Valve and Fitting Distributors Finance Cross-Border Inventory Through Laredo A valve distributor in Texas lives on lead times, and valve fitting importer financing in Texas has to keep pace with them. An industrial customer needs 400 units of a specific ball valve, the vendor across the border can build them in six weeks, and the truck can cross at Laredo in a matter of days once they are ready. The goods move fast. The money moves first. That gap is the whole problem, and it is why Laredo import financing exists as a category of its own. You pay the vendor to start production, then wait for a customer who pays on 45 or 60 day terms after delivery. The border crossing itself is the quickest part of the journey. Why Laredo Changed the Math for Texas Valve and Fitting Distributors Laredo is the Western Hemisphere's leading land port. Port Laredo recorded $353.94 billion in international trade in 2025 , which also places it among the top three US ports of entry by trade value. More to the point for Mexico cross border trade finance : machinery and industrial components make up a large share of what crosses here. Valves, fittings, couplings, and the hardware that goes with them travel this corridor, which means the vendor base on the Mexican side is deep and the crossing itself is short. Short transit does not mean short cash cycles Here is where distributors get caught. Ocean freight from Asia can run several weeks, so the cash cycle feels obviously long and gets planned for. A truck from Monterrey arrives in two days, which makes the whole transaction feel fast. But the vendor still wants a deposit before production starts, production still takes weeks, and your customer still pays 45 days after delivery. The truck is fast. The money is not. Congestion is a real scheduling risk Crossing times at Laredo move with volume, inspection load, and the season, and commercial queues can lengthen without much warning. For a distributor promising a delivery date, that variability is worth financing around, and a reason Laredo import financing gets sized with some slack in it. By the numbers Port Laredo, by the numbers $353.94B in international trade moved through Port Laredo in 2025 Top 3 US port of entry by trade value 97% of Port Laredo's trade is tied directly to Mexico 42% of financing applicants received the full amount they sought Sources: Port Laredo 2025 trade release; Federal Reserve Banks, 2026 Report on Employer Firms ![where the cash gap opens on a cross-border order](https://images.ctfassets.net/vkoe68wv76dt/4BE02DW8Y3myp9OYlChgVQ/8c497ac77cddc44d88f19630952f3de6/infographic-1-cash-gap-timeline) The Three Places Cash Gets Stuck Cross-border distribution ties up money in a few predictable spots, and each one shapes how valve fitting importer financing in Texas gets structured. The vendor deposit before production Custom or semi-custom industrial hardware usually needs a deposit at order. The vendor is committing machine time and raw material, so the money goes out before anything exists. For a growing distributor, several open orders at once can absorb most of the available cash, which is the usual trigger for seeking Texas valve distributor funding . Inventory sitting in the warehouse Nearshoring means shorter lead times, which tempts distributors to hold more line items instead of fewer. That is good for winning orders and hard on working capital. Stock on the shelf is cash you have already spent. Customer payment terms after delivery Industrial buyers, contractors, and MRO accounts pay on terms. Net 45 or net 60 terms are common in the industry, and they start after delivery, not after you paid the vendor. Add the production window and the total gap can stretch across several months, which is a working capital problem more than a sales problem. Importer Financing Options for Valve and Fitting Distributors A few trade finance options fit this pattern, and they solve different pieces of Mexico cross border trade finance . Vendor Financing Vendor Financing pays your vendor directly so production can start without your cash leaving the business. You repay within an agreed window, typically up to ninety days, which gives the goods time to cross, get delivered, and start turning into an invoice. Pricing is a flat fee on the invoice, applied only to what you draw and only while it stays outstanding. For most Laredo import financing needs, that covers the production leg. A Line of Credit A Line of Credit suits the distributor who is placing orders continuously. You draw when a deposit comes due, repay over six installments, and draw again for the next order, without setting up new financing each time. That makes it a practical shape for Texas valve distributor funding when you are buying every month. It works differently from a term loan or bank loan , where the full sum arrives at once. Negotiating better terms directly Worth trying before financing. A vendor you have bought from for years may accept a smaller deposit or longer terms. Our guide to extending vendor payment terms covers how to ask. That costs nothing and works until your order volume outgrows what the vendor is willing to carry. Your vendor needs paying before the bridge . Drip Capital pays your vendor in Mexico directly, so a deposit deadline does not compete with payroll. No collateral required. Talk to Drip Capital → $9B+ trade financed • 11,000+ businesses served • 100+ countries What Texas Distributors Should Have Ready Having the paperwork ready avoids avoidable delays. Vendor Financing also requires a minimum of two years in business, so factor that in before you apply. Have the confirmed purchase order, the vendor's invoice or pro forma showing cost of goods, your business formation documents, and recent bank statements. Cross-border deals also benefit from clean customs documentation, since a broker delay can push out the whole timeline and slow any valve fitting importer financing in Texas application along with it. How Drip Capital Helps Cross-Border Importers Drip Capital pays your vendor in Mexico directly, so a deposit deadline does not compete with payroll. Repayment falls within an agreed window, typically up to ninety days, and the cost is a flat fee on the invoice rather than a rate that shifts on you. There is no collateral required, which matters for owners who would rather not pledge business assets behind an inventory purchase. Vendor Financing through Drip Capital asks for a minimum of two years in business, and the strength of the order and your vendor relationship carries real weight in approval. Frequently Asked Questions Why do Texas distributors importing through Laredo still need financing if the crossing itself is quick? Transit time is the shortest part of the cycle, which is the point most Laredo import financing conversations start from. The vendor needs a deposit before production, production takes weeks, and your customer pays 45 to 60 days after delivery. The cash gap comes from those stages, not the border crossing. Does financing help with customs or broker delays? Not directly, though it reduces the damage. If a shipment sits longer than planned, financing means your own cash is not the thing waiting, so a delay becomes a scheduling problem instead of a payroll problem. What financing fits a distributor placing orders every month? A Line of Credit generally suits recurring purchasing and is one route to Texas valve distributor funding , since the facility stays open between orders. Vendor Financing fits when the priority is getting a specific vendor paid so production can start. Do I need to pledge collateral or sign a personal guarantee to finance cross-border inventory? Not with Drip Capital's Vendor Financing, which is collateral-free and requires no personal guarantee, so Mexico cross border trade finance need not put your personal assets behind an inventory order. Terms vary by provider, so confirm this specifically with anyone else you compare.

title: CACI’s SkyValor Selected to Strengthen Drone Defense at the Southern Border
summary: CACI advances SkyValor into full-rate production to rapidly expand delivery of its proven drone defense capability Reston, Va., July 13 – CACI International Inc (NYSE: CACI) announced today that...
body_text: News Releases Download PDF Company Release - 07/13/2026 CACI’s SkyValor Selected to Strengthen Drone Defense at the Southern Border CACI advances SkyValor into full-rate production to rapidly expand delivery of its proven drone defense capability Reston, Va., July 13 – CACI International Inc (NYSE: CACI) announced today that it was awarded a contract by the Department of War (DoW) to deploy SkyValor, CACI’s advanced drone defense system, at the Southern Border. The deployment will support a broader national security effort to counter the growing threat of hostile drones and strengthen homeland defense in high-priority operating environments. “Drone threats are evolving quickly, and they are challenging the way we protect our forces, borders, and critical infrastructure,” said John Mengucci , CACI President and Chief Executive Officer. “SkyValor gives defenders the advantage with earlier warning, faster decisions, and precise defeat of hostile drones with low-to-no collateral impact. With successful operational evaluations complete, we are moving SkyValor into full-rate production to deliver this capability at the speed our customers need.” Under the contract, CACI will deliver SkyValor as a transportable drone defense system that can be deployed rapidly where protection is needed most. SkyValor combines advanced sensing, automated defeat capabilities, and decades of counter-drone experience to find, track, and stop hostile drones—including cellular-enabled drones—before they can threaten national security operations. SkyValor gives warfighters and homeland defenders the precision needed to stay ahead of rapidly evolving drone threats. About CACI CACI International Inc (NYSE: CACI) is a technology-first national security company with 27,000 talented employees. We expand the limits of national security through innovation, discipline, and operational excellence. We ensure our customers’ success by delivering technologies to accelerate innovation, drive speed and efficiency, and rapidly anticipate and eliminate threats.
